title: Payment Arrangements Policy — One Arrangement per Placed Account
content:
## Clause

1. A consumer may hold one payment arrangement per placed account and any number of arrangements across different placed accounts; one arrangement never covers more than one account.
2. A new plan is set up only when no other plan on the same placed account is in pending authorization, active, suspended or broken status.
3. A consumer who wants new terms on an account whose plan is still open must first have that plan cancelled or completed; a broken plan is either reinstated or cancelled under the breakage rule before any new plan.

There is no limit on the number of Payment Arrangements one consumer holds across different placed accounts; the limit is one open plan per placed account.

## Evidence and object

Whether another plan is open on the account is read from Ridgeline's own plan records, before the new plan is set up, matching plans by the placed account the new plan would pay. A consumer's own account of what is open does not replace the records. Plans on the consumer's other placed accounts are not counted against this account.

## Status table for the same placed account

| Status of an existing plan on the same placed account | Effect on setting up a new plan |
|---|---|
| Pending authorization | Blocks a new plan |
| Active | Blocks a new plan |
| Suspended | Blocks a new plan |
| Broken | Blocks a new plan (the broken plan is reinstated or cancelled under the breakage rule first) |
| Completed | Not counted by this rule |
| Cancelled | Not counted by this rule |

## Hypothetical cases

- A consumer owes three placed accounts, one with an active Standard Installment Plan. A new plan may be considered on either of the other two accounts; on the first account no new plan is set up while the active plan stands.
- An account's only earlier plan shows completed: that plan is not counted by this rule.
- An account carries one plan in broken status: no new plan is set up on that account while the broken plan remains in that status.
